beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: A digital clock jittering between irregular timestamps, failing to sync with a steady pulse.

beats.text: Mamba forces the time-step to be a function of the input, like a musician who speeds up their metronome every time they play a loud note.
beats.visual_focus: A metronome arm swinging erratically, desyncing from a constant, linear timeline.

beats.text: Enter TIDES: it keeps the physical time gap constant, shifting the input-dependence from the step size to the diagonal state matrix instead.
beats.visual_focus: A matrix transformation animation showing the diagonal elements shifting while the time-step remains locked.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was actually sick—calling out the 'broken internal clock' of current models made me stop scrolling immediately. I liked the Mamba metronome analogy, it made the time-step issue click instantly. I got a bit lost on the math in Beat 4; 'projecting the input onto the diagonal' sounds like a heavy linear algebra operation that needs a tiny bit more context on why that specifically fixes the continuous-time issue.
